sentences.text: 4. The facts leading rise to the present contempt application are that an Original Suit No.1092 of 1995 was filed by the applicant for specific performance of agreement dated 18.07.1994 executed between the applicant and one Hari Ram.
The suit was decreed on 31.03.1998.
Against the said judgment and decree, a First Appeal was preferred by Hari Ram, which was dismissed on 29.8.1998.
Thereafter, a second appeal was filed before this Court which was also dismissed on 16.11.1998.

The matter travelled up to the Apex Court through special leave petition being preferred by Hari Ram,
which was dismissed on 19.02.1999.

Thereafter a review application was moved by Hari Ram which was also dismissed by the Apex Court on 15.7.1999.
5.
It seems that during pendency of these proceedings, an execution case was filed by the applicant.

The execution proceedings were contested by Hari Ram, which was ultimately upheld in favour of the applicant by the order of the writ Court dated 11.9.2014 passed in Writ-C No.26023 of 2007,
which is as under :
"Heard Sri Vineet Kumar Sahu, learned counsel for the petitioner and Ms. Abhilasha Singh, learned counsel for respondent no. 1.
O.S. No. 1092 of 1995 has been filed by respondent no. 1 for specific performance of the agreement dated 18.07.1994.
The suit was decreed on 31.03.1998.
The appeal filed against the decree, was dismissed on 29.08.1998.
Second Appeal was dismissed on 16.11.1998 and the Special Leave Petition filed by the petitioner, was dismissed on 19.02.1999.
Against that order, review application was filed by the petitioner, which was dismissed on 15.07.1999 by the Apex Court.
After dismissal of the review application, an application dated 03.04.1999 was filed by the decree holder for execution of the decree.

An objection dated 20.08.1999 was filed by the petitioner in execution and simultaneously, an application under Section 28 of Specific Relief Act was filed, which was allowed on 25.08.1999 by the executing Court.
Challenging the order dated 25.08.1999, the decree holder filed a revision, which was allowed on 25.08.1999 and the matter has been remitted back to the executing Court.
Another application under Section 28 of Specific Relief Act was moved by the petitioner, which was dismissed on 04.08.2000.
The decree holder was given 15 days time to deposit the amount Rs. 23,000/- of the sale consideration.
Pursuant thereto the said amount was deposited by the decree holder on 07.08.2000 in the Court.

In the meantime, the petitioner filed a Writ Petition No. 37334 of 2000 challenging the order dated 04.08.2000, which was dismissed vide judgment and order dated 24.05.2001 with costs.
After the dismissals of the writ petition, the execution case had proceeded for execution of the sale deed.

The petitioner then moved an application under Section 47 CPC with the objection that the decree was not executable inasmuch as the Satveer And 2 Others vs Smt. Sharbati And 5 Others on 29 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94574960/

sentences.text: proceeding for acquisition of the suit property had been initiated by the State Government.
The execution court has accepted the objection of the petitioner and allowed the application under Section 47 CPC vide order dated 04.02.2002.
It was held that the decree was not executable.

Challenging the order dated 04.02.2002,
Revision No. 116 of 2002 was filed by the decree holder, which was allowed on 19.12.2005.

It has been observed by the revisional Court that despite the decree holder having won the litigation up to Supreme Court, the decree in his favour could not be executed for one or the other reason on objections being raised by the petitioners/
judgment debtor.

It was observed that the executing court has categorically erred in allowing the application under section 47 CPC for the reason that the application has been filed only on the ground that the notification under section 28 and 29 of U.P.
Awas Evam Vikas Act have been issued.

The executing Court has wrongly relied upon a letter of the Executive Engineer to Sub Divisional Officer (Finance and Revenue)
not to register the sale deeds in view of the proposed acquisition.
Revision No. 116 of 2002 was allowed on 19.12.2005 and the matter was remitted back.

The executing court again on an application under section 47 CPC moved by the petitioner on the ground that now the proceedings for acquisition of the suit property has been initiated, a notification under section 17 (1) of the Land Acquisition Act has been issued and the name of the State of U.P. has been recorded in the revenue record in place of Hari Ram i.e. the petitioner, and notice under section 9 has also been issued and the possession has been taken on 23.11.2006, has allowed the objection.

It was held that as the suit property has been vested in the State Government under Section 16 of Land Acquisition Act, the decree was not executable against the petitioner as the petitioner/ judgment debtor now cannot execute the sale deed in favour of the decree holder.
Aggrieved a revision was filed which was allowed on 09.05.2007.
Hence this petition.
The revisional court after consideration of the objections filed by the petitioner has come to the conclusion that decree has been affirmed by the Apex Court.
The execution case has been filed in the year 1998 after the decree was affirmed.

Now,
only question remains as to whether in the changed circumstances it is proper to execute the sale deed pursuant to the decree passed by the court below, which has been held valid by the highest Court of this Country.

In view of the above, it was held that even if the proceedings of the land acquisition has become final and the land has been acquired, the decree holder is entitled for compensation being owner of the suit property on the date of notification for acquisition, and hence the conclusion drawn by the executing court that the decree was not executable was clearly erroneous.
The revision was allowed and the order dated 09.02.2007 passed by the Executing Court was set-aside.

sentences.text: Challenging the order passed by the revisional court, learned counsel for the petitioner placed reliance upon a copy of the agreement dated 18.07.1994 which has been filed along with the supplementary rejoinder affidavit dated 07.02.2013.

Placing reliance on the averments made in paragraph 7 of the supplementary rejoinder affidavit, learned counsel for the petitioner submits that on the basis of a forged document i.e. agreement dated 18.07.1994, the decree holder has succeeded in getting the decree in his favour.
The decree cannot be executed on the basis of a forged document.
The petitioner is a judgment debtor and the decree has been upheld by the Supreme Court in the SLP filed by him.
As the decree has attained finality, it is not open for the petitioner to challenge the validity of the same.

Moreover, it is apparent from the record that the petitioner despite being a judgment debtor and the decree having become final as far back in July, 1999, when the review application filed by the petitioner has been dismissed by the Supreme Court has succeeded in delaying the execution of the decree.
After the execution application was filed on 03.04.1999, the petitioner/judgment debtor moved various applications one after the other in order to stall the execution of the decree.
The decree holder had performed his part of the decree and has deposited the remaining consideration in the court below.

The executing court has clearly erred in passing the order dated 09.02.2007 holding that the decree was not executable as the suit property has been acquired and hence the application for execution of the decree was liable to be rejected.
The revisional court has rightly held that as the decree has become final, the question would be of apportionment of compensation for the acquired land.
The decree holder has wrongly been deprived of the compensation for acquisition of the suit property of which he has become owner on the basis of the decree of a civil court.

On the date of issuance of the notification for acquisition the decree has attained finality and only the execution application was pending and further the consideration for execution of the sale deed has already been deposited by the decree holder.
In view of the above, the order dated 09.05.2007 passed by the revisional court is affirmed being justified.

Learned counsel for respondent no. 1 decree holder submits that after the order dated 09.05.2007 passed by the revisional court, a review application was filed during pendency of the present writ petition.
The said review application was allowed by order dated 15.12.2007.

Challenging the order dated 15.12.2007, Writ Petition No.
51277 of 2008 (Man Singh vs. Addl. District Judge and others) was filed by respondent no. 1, which was allowed on 05.04.2012.

sentences.text: In view of the fact that the respondent/decree holder had initiated execution proceedings in the year 1999 after it was affirmed by the Apex Court and the petitioner/ judgment debtor has succeeded in dragging him in several rounds of litigation from the court below up to this Court from the year 1999 to 2014, the writ petitions is, dismissed with costs which I quantity to Rs. 20,000/-, payable to the decree holder within one month.

The writ petition is accordingly dismissed with costs."

During pendency of the said writ petition, the applicant had filed Writ-C No.5177 of 2008 requiring that the decree be executed by the Court below.

The writ Court on 5.4.2012 had passed the following order :-
"
Heard Sri Siddharth Verma, learned counsel for the petitioner.
This is a peculiar case where the decree holder who is the petitioner herein in spite of having a decree in his favour has been unable to get it executed, in the circumstances, narrated hereinafter.
The petitioner-plaintiff filed a suit for specific performance against the respondent No. 4, Hari Ram on the basis of an agreement to sell.
The suit was decreed in his favour throughout and the judgment and decree of Trial Court has been affirmed up to the Apex Court.
The execution proceedings commenced in the year 1999 and till date the decree could not be executed on account of the pending litigation as unfolded in the writ petition.
During the pendency of the execution proceedings the land in dispute which was subject matter of the judgment and decree came to be acquired by the Avas Vikas Parishad.
The execution was thereafter resisted by Hari Ram on several grounds including the ground that since the land has now been acquired, the sale deed cannot be executed.
The Executing Court allowed the said application against which the petitioner-plaintiff filed a revision.

The learned Additional District Judge, Court No. 1 Ghaziabad set aside the order of the executing Court on 09.05.2007 holding that it is true that land having been acquired by the Avas Vikas Parishad, the said sale deed cannot be executed but under the changed circumstances the plaintiff-petitioner was entitled to receive compensation in place of respondent No. 4, the defendant in the suit.

Hari Ram aggrieved by the order dated 9th May, 2007 filed writ petition No. 26023 of 2007.
The records of the said writ petition have been placed alongwith the present writ petition which discloses that writ petition has been dismissed for non-prosecution on 15th April, 2009.

The respondent No. 5 Hari Singh S/o Shankar, thereafter appears to have filed an application that the order dated 9th May, 2007 has been passed ex-parte to him and since his interest is involved, the said order deserves to be reviewed.
It is at the instance of the respondent No. 5 that now the impugned order has been passed by the Additional District Judge, Ghaziabad dated 15.12.2007.
This Court entertained the present writ petition filed by the petitioner-plaintiff assailing the aforesaid order dated 15.12.2007 and the operation thereof was stayed on 28.01.2008.
Notices were issued and the undelivered cover was returned back to this Court with an endorsement that in spite of search being made nothing was known about the whereabouts of Opposite Party No. 5.
The said office report is dated 24th April,2008.
The Opposite Party No. 4 had been also sent a notice and the undelivered cover with the acknowledgment has not been returned back.
The petitioner-plaintiff in these circumstances, moved an application being application No. 138032 of 2008 praying for service of notice on the said respondents by publication in the newspaper.
This Court passed an order on 15th April, 2009 allowing the petitioner to get the notices published in a widely circulated newspaper of district Ghaziabad.

The petitioner thereafter, filed an affidavit of service dated 27th May, 2009 enclosing the copy of Hindi Daily Rashtriya Sahara dated 21st April, 2009 that incorporates the notice as directed by this Court.

Having perused the said affidavit and in view of the provisions of Rule 20 of Order 5 Civil Procedure Code read with the rules of the High Court, 1952, the said service is treated to be sufficient on Opposite Party No. 4 and 5.
In the circumstances, the aforesaid and the facts as brought on record.
The respondent No. 4 and 5 have failed to respond to the writ petition in spite of all steps having been taken for service of notice.
I have heard learned counsel for the petitioner Sri Siddhartha Verma and perused the impugned order.
In the opinion of the Court, the Court below has committed an error by treating the order having been passed against a dead person Badlu.
Badlu was the person who sold the land to Hari Ram and had no surviving interest left.

Even for the sake of arguments that the respondent No. 5 Hari Singh is related to Badlu, nothing remained to be contested by him in the aforesaid circumstances when the defendant Hari Ram had already lost the battle up to the Apex Court.

Needless to say and as noted above the writ petition filed by Hari Ram against the order dated 9th May, 2007 already stood dismissed as a result whereof the order dated 9th May, 2007 stood upheld by the High Court.
In such circumstances, there was no reason to recall or review the order dated 9th May, 2007.

7. Today, when the case was taken up, learned counsel for the applicant submitted that though the compensation for the land acquired by U.P. Awas Avam Vikas Parishad had been paid, but, the additional land of 5% had not been given.
He contends that the orders of the writ Court of the years 2012 as well as 2014 have been violated and the officers of the U.P. Awas Avam Vikas Parishad should be punished.

8. Sri Vivek Saran, counsel appearing for U.P. Awas Avam Vikas Parishad submits that dispute was between the two private person for the land in question which was acquired by U.P. Awas Avam Vikas Parishad.
The suit filed by the applicant was decreed by the Court below which was affirmed by the order of Hon'ble Apex Court in the year 1999.
As the suit was decreed, the compensation has been paid to the applicant.
9. I have heard the respective counsel for the parties and perused the material on record.
10. From perusal of the material on record, it is clear that it is an inter-se dispute between the applicant and one Hari Ram.
The lis was decided by the orders of Hon'ble Apex Court.
The matter had travelled upto the execution proceedings which were finalized and the decree was executed.
The compensation has been paid by the U.P.Awas Avam Vikas Parishad, which is admitted to the applicant.

11. The question of giving 5% extra land cannot be dealt with while deciding the contempt proceedings as that was not subject matter in the writ petition filed by one Hari Ram or in the writ petition filed by applicant in the year 2008.
It was an inter se dispute between the two private person which had travelled up to this Court and the writ Court had decided the writ petition on 05.04.2012 and 11.9.2014.
12. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, I find that no case for contempt is made out.

The applicant has deliberately impleaded the officials of U.P. Awas Avam Vikas Parishad as there was no direction either in the order of the writ Court dated 05.4.2012 against them or in the order of the writ Court dated 11.9.2014.

The writ Court, while dismissing the writ petition filed by Hari Ram,
on 11.9.2014 had upheld the revisional order dated 09.5.2007 and had dismissed the writ petition with a cost of Rs.20,000/-.
Similarly, the writ petition No.5177 of 2008 was allowed and the order impugned therein was quashed.

There was no direction or order against the officials of the U.P.
Awas Avam Vikas Parishad or U.P. Awas Avam Vikas Parishad itself.
13. In view of the above, I find that no case for contempt is made out as the applicant has wrongly dragged the officials of U.P. Awas Avam Vikas Parishad in the contempt proceedings.
